findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it an internet-routable endpoint instead of confining it to the VPC. Combined with the predictable 'admin' master user and credentials embedded elsewhere in this configuration, the database is directly exposed to untrusted networks.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume, snapshots and automated backups, so all database contents are stored in cleartext at the storage layer.

The master password is supplied via var.password and is also interpolated into the EC2 user_data, so the plaintext credential is persisted in Terraform state and in instance metadata rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager or the RDS managed master password. lifecycle ignore_changes on password additionally suppresses rotation through Terraform.

Neither the instance nor its parameter group enforces TLS for client connections (no require_secure_transport), and the application connects with plain mysqli_connect, so credentials and query data can traverse the network unencrypted — significant given the instance is publicly accessible.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced in parameter group
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and omits require_secure_transport = 1, so the attached publicly accessible database accepts unencrypted client connections.

The user_data script writes the RDS master username and the raw value of var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable in cleartext from the instance metadata service by anyone with an SSRF or code-execution foothold on the internet-facing PHP application, and by any principal with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute.

No metadata_options block is set (http_tokens = "required"), so IMDSv1 remains enabled. The instance hosts a public-facing PHP application and carries a highly privileged instance profile, so a single SSRF can retrieve role credentials and the plaintext user_data secrets.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance volume — which stores the database credentials file /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc — may be created unencrypted unless account-level EBS default encryption is enabled.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". It is attached via aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2profile to a web-facing EC2 instance, so compromise of the PHP application yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases in the account, including privilege escalation via instance launch and RDS snapshot exfiltration.

Port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than only to the application instance's security group (aws_security_group.web-node), so any workload anywhere in the VPC can reach the database directly, weakening tier segmentation.

The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, removing an egress control that would otherwise constrain data exfiltration or callback traffic from a compromised database tier.
